metadata.case_name: YIM FAT FONG v. WONG KIM HUNG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: self employed business as a poultry dealer supplying chickens, ducks and geese to, for the most part, restaurants and, to a lesser extent, cooked meat stalls

injuries.description: fracture dislocation of the 6th and 7th cervical vertebrae
source: the Plaintiff suffered a fracture dislocation of the 6th and 7th cervical vertebrae which was treated with open reduction and metal wire fixation approximately one week after admission to hospital.
There was a head injury with no apparent brain damage or lesion - a scalp laceration needed suturing
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

source: as a result of the injuries he became subject to epileptiform attacks which after much variation in type of drugs and dosage, came under a degree of control.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

manifestations.description: numbness over his fingers, especially those of his right hand
clumsy gait, being prone to fall
absent tendon reflexes in the left arms and upper abdominal reflexes
mild weakness and numbness in the left hand and arm
degree of disability in the legs
sensory loss to the index and middle fingers bilaterally
well-preserved muscle power in the upper limbs (clinical finding)

treatments_received.treatment: open reduction and metal wire fixation (spinal fusion)
source: the Plaintiff suffered a fracture dislocation of the 6th and 7th cervical vertebrae which was treated with open reduction and metal wire fixation approximately one week after admission to hospital.

treatments_received.treatment: bone grafts taken from his iliac crest
source: after undergoing the spinal fusion for which bone grafts were taken from his iliac crest, he was transferred from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital to the Kowloon Hospital for rehabilitation with a halo-body jacket to immobilise his neck.

treatments_received.treatment: halo-body jacket to immobilise his neck (rehabilitation)
source: he was transferred from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital to the Kowloon Hospital for rehabilitation with a halo-body jacket to immobilise his neck.

treatments_received.treatment: anticonvulsant / antiepileptic medication (examples recorded: Luminal, Phenytoin (Dilantin), Mysolin, Epilim, Tegretol)
source: The Nursing Kardex entry for the evening of 24th March reads - "Dr. W. H. Li - Luminal 30 mgs. Phenytoin (dilantin) 100 mgs. Mysolin 250 mgs. N.P.O. (nil by mouth) except medication"
He was obliquely critical of the hospital treatment which increased his dose of Epilim on top of a large dose of Tegretol when writing in July 1998.

treatments_future.treatment: psychiatric treatment: one session a month for one year
source: I will allow for one session a month for one year. Any benefit to be achieved from it will be realised within that period.

losses.description: A little over five years ago he met with an accident which effectively put an end to his self employed business as a poultry dealer supplying chickens, ducks and geese to, for the most part, restaurants and, to a lesser extent, cooked meat stalls.
